value: Anne possesses a vivid imagination.
unit: Possessing a vivid imagination and an intense passion for beauty, Anne is an imaginative dreamer who weaves romantic fancies into the world around her. She has a deep capacity for affection and a strong desire to be loved, placing great value on kindred spirits and true friendship. Though quick-tempered and impulsive when provoked, particularly regarding her looks, she is generous, warm-hearted, and forgiving. She approaches life with an irrepressible enthusiasm and optimism, striving earnestly to live up to her high ideals.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley was brought to Green Gables in Avonlea by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert.
unit: Anne Shirley was mistakenly brought to Green Gables in Avonlea by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert, who had intended to adopt a boy from an orphan asylum. Though initially reluctant, Marilla agreed to keep her. Anne quickly formed a passionate friendship with Diana Barry and developed a fierce rivalry with classmate Gilbert Blythe after he called her 'Carrots.' After two years of studying under Miss Stacy, she tied for first place on the entrance exams for Queen's Academy, where she subsequently won the Avery Scholarship. Following Matthew's sudden death, Anne gave up the scholarship to remain at Green Gables and support Marilla, taking the post of teacher at Avonlea School. During her two years as a teacher, she founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, helped Marilla raise the orphaned Keith twins, and reconciled her long-standing feud with Gilbert, becoming his close friend. After Mrs. Rachel Lynde moved into Green Gables to live with Marilla, Anne was able to attend Redmond College in Kingsport alongside Gilbert, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon. While at Redmond, she rented Patty's Place, rejected a proposal from Roy Gardner after realizing she did not love him, and graduated with High Honors in English. Admitting her love for Gilbert when he nearly died of typhoid fever, she accepted his proposal of marriage in Hester Gray's garden. They were married in the orchard at Green Gables and moved to a little white house on Four Winds Harbor, where Gilbert established his medical practice. There they suffered the loss of their firstborn infant daughter, Joyce, before welcoming a healthy son, James Matthew.

Though initially reluctant, Marilla agreed to keep her. Anne quickly formed a passionate friendship with Diana Barry and developed a fierce rivalry with classmate Gilbert Blythe after he called her 'Carrots.' After two years of studying under Miss Stacy, she tied for first place on the entrance exams for Queen's Academy, where she subsequently won the Avery Scholarship. Following Matthew's sudden death, Anne gave up the scholarship to remain at Green Gables and support Marilla, taking the post of teacher at Avonlea School. During her two years as a teacher, she founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, helped Marilla raise the orphaned Keith twins, and reconciled her long-standing feud with Gilbert, becoming his close friend. After Mrs. Rachel Lynde moved into Green Gables to live with Marilla, Anne was able to attend Redmond College in Kingsport alongside Gilbert, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon. While at Redmond, she rented Patty's Place, rejected a proposal from Roy Gardner after realizing she did not love him, and graduated with High Honors in English. Admitting her love for Gilbert when he nearly died of typhoid fever, she accepted his proposal of marriage in Hester Gray's garden. They were married in the orchard at Green Gables and moved to a little white house on Four Winds Harbor, where Gilbert established his medical practice. There they suffered the loss of their firstborn infant daughter, Joyce, before welcoming a healthy son, James Matthew.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye comes to Avonlea
unit: Anthony Pye comes to Avonlea as an orphan to live with his uncle, Mr. George Pye. When Anne Shirley takes over Avonlea School, Anthony quickly sets himself against her, expressing contempt for female teachers. He constantly misbehaves, whispering, making faces, and mocking her instruction. Anne attempts to win his affection through patience and gentleness, but Anthony remains unimpressed and resistant. His antagonism reaches a climax when he secretly places a live mouse in Anne's desk drawer. After being caught and openly confessing with insolence, Anne loses her temper and chastises him with her pointer. Following this punishment, Anthony's attitude changes significantly; he begins showing respect for Anne, even offering to carry her books, and admits that her whipping was as good as a man's.

value: Aunt Jamesina agreed to move to Kingsport.
unit: Aunt Jamesina agreed to move to Kingsport and act as housekeeper for her niece Stella, along with Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon at Patty's Place. During their college years at Redmond, she provided a warm, motherly home for the girls while letting them live independently. She cared deeply for the house's three cats—Joseph, the Sarah-cat, and Rusty—and chose to remain in Kingsport during holiday breaks to look after them. After the girls graduated from Redmond, she decided to take the three cats to her own home to live with her.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea
unit: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school. As a young man, he admired Anne Shirley and drove her, along with Jane and Diana, to a concert at the White Sands Hotel, though he decamped before the supper due to his shyness. When his father gave him the upper farm, he wished to marry Anne, but was too bashful to propose himself. He persuaded his sister Jane to propose to Anne on his behalf. After Anne rejected the proposal, Billy did not break his heart and soon married Nettie Blewett, settling down on his farm in Avonlea.

label: History
value: Captain Jim Boyd ran away to sea as a young lad.
unit: Captain Jim Boyd, born and raised at Four Winds, ran away to sea as a young lad and spent the majority of his life as a sailor, travelling to the far corners of the earth and surviving innumerable perils. In his youth he fell in love with a girl named Margaret, but she tragically vanished at sea during a sudden squall, an event that shaped his emotional life forever as he remained devoted to her memory. Eventually retiring from the sea, he became the keeper of the Four Winds Light at the harbor entrance. When Gilbert and Anne Blythe moved to the shore, Captain Jim immediately befriended them as 'kindred spirits.' He welcomed Owen Ford, the grandson of his old friend the schoolmaster, and collaborated with him by providing his lifelong journal to be written into 'The Life-Book of Captain Jim.' Captain Jim also took a deep interest in Leslie Moore's welfare, having been the one to find her husband in Cuba years prior. After seeing his 'life-book' published and receiving his first printed copy, Captain Jim passed away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse, his hands resting on the opened manuscript.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman is nicknamed 'Charlotta the Fourth' by Miss Lavendar Lewis.
unit: Leonora Bowman, nicknamed 'Charlotta the Fourth' by Miss Lavendar Lewis, entered service at Echo Lodge to assist with housekeeping. She developed a deep affection for Miss Lavendar and befriended Anne Shirley and Diana Barry upon their visits. She assisted in entertaining guests, including Paul Irving and Stephen Irving. When Stephen Irving returned to marry Miss Lavendar, Charlotta enthusiastically helped prepare Echo Lodge for the wedding. At the ceremony, she threw an old shoe for luck, accidentally striking the minister, Mr. Allan. Following the wedding, she helped pack up Echo Lodge and arranged to move to Boston with Mr. and Mrs. Irving.

label: Personality
value: Cornelia Bryant is an outspoken woman.
unit: Cornelia Bryant is an outspoken, sharp-tongued, and fiercely independent woman who prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor. She holds strong, outspoken prejudices, particularly against men and Methodists, often expressing a humorous yet sharp contempt for masculine foibles. Beneath her blunt, critical exterior and caustic wit lies a profoundly kind, charitable, and helpful heart, as she is always among the first to offer practical aid to those in distress.

label: History
value: Cornelia Bryant lived as a prominent spinster at Four Winds.
unit: Cornelia Bryant lived for many years as a prominent, outspoken spinster at Four Winds, known throughout the area for her sharp tongue, her vehement distaste for men and Methodists, and her untiring neighborly kindness. She was a close friend and protector of Leslie Moore, whom she supported through her tragic life and marriage. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe moved to the house of dreams at Four Winds Harbor, Cornelia quickly befriended Anne, becoming a frequent visitor and a constant source of local news, sharp humor, and practical help. After maintaining her anti-matrimonial stance for decades, Cornelia surprised her friends by agreeing to marry her longtime suitor, Marshall Elliott, after he finally shaved his beard upon the election of the Liberal government. Following their marriage, Marshall moved into her home, where Cornelia continued her active involvement in church and community affairs, including taking the orphaned Mary Vance into her home to raise.

label: History
value: Davy Keith and Dora are twins.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora were orphaned when their mother Mary Keith died in East Grafton. As their uncle in British Columbia could not immediately take them, Marilla Cuthbert agreed to take the twins into Green Gables. Davy quickly established a reputation for chaotic mischief and endless questioning, testing the patience of Marilla and Mrs. Rachel Lynde while developing a deep affection for Anne Shirley. Over time, his behavior gradually improved under Anne's gentle guidance and understanding, despite occasional pranks like trapping his sister in an outhouse, putting a toad in Marilla's bed, and stealing plum jam. Following the death of his uncle Richard Keith, a trust fund was provided for the twins, ensuring they would remain permanently at Green Gables. Davy eventually started attending Avonlea school, becoming close friends with Milty Boulter and engaging in typical boyhood rivalries and misadventures. As he grew older, he developed an interest in farming and continued to be a lively, loving presence at Green Gables.

label: History
value: Diana Barry grows up at Orchard Slope
unit: Diana Barry grows up at Orchard Slope near Green Gables and becomes Anne Shirley's bosom friend after taking a solemn vow of eternal loyalty. Their early friendship faces a trial when Diana accidentally drinks currant wine at Green Gables, leading her mother to temporarily forbid them from playing together. The friendship is fully restored after Anne helps save Diana's little sister, Minnie May, during a bout of croup. Diana attends Avonlea School alongside Anne, participating in the Story Club, the Debating Club concert, and the school's Christmas performance. She later attends Queen's Academy, though she chooses not to pursue a teaching career. After completing her studies, Diana settles in Avonlea and becomes engaged to Fred Wright. They marry in a grand ceremony at Orchard Slope, with Anne serving as her bridesmaid. The couple makes their home in Avonlea, where Diana gives birth to her children, including her eldest son, Fred, and a daughter named Small Anne Cordelia.

label: History
value: Dick Moore grew up at Four Winds
unit: Dick Moore grew up at Four Winds as the son of Abner Moore. As a young man, he worked in his father's store during the winter and went to sea in the summer. He became enamored with Leslie West and, through his father holding a heavy mortgage on the West farm, coercively induced her mother to force Leslie into marrying him when she was sixteen. Following their marriage, he lived with Leslie on the West farm for a winter before leaving in the spring on a voyage to Cuba aboard the ship Four Sisters. While in Cuba, Dick contracted yellow fever and died. His cousin, George Moore, stayed behind to nurse him, leaving the ship to sail without them. Shortly after Dick's death, George suffered a traumatic brain injury in a brawling accident that destroyed his memory and intellect. When Captain Jim later found the brain-damaged George in Havana, he mistook him for Dick due to their striking physical resemblance and brought him back to Four Winds, where Leslie nursed him for twelve years believing him to be her husband. The truth was finally discovered when Dr. Gilbert Blythe suggested a trephining operation, which restored George Moore's memory and revealed that the real Dick Moore had died thirteen years prior.

unit: Dick Moore grew up at Four Winds as the son of Abner Moore. As a young man, he worked in his father's store during the winter and went to sea in the summer. He became enamored with Leslie West and, through his father holding a heavy mortgage on the West farm, coercively induced her mother to force Leslie into marrying him when she was sixteen. Following their marriage, he lived with Leslie on the West farm for a winter before leaving in the spring on a voyage to Cuba aboard the ship Four Sisters. While in Cuba, Dick contracted yellow fever and died. His cousin, George Moore, stayed behind to nurse him, leaving the ship to sail without them. Shortly after Dick's death, George suffered a traumatic brain injury in a brawling accident that destroyed his memory and intellect. When Captain Jim later found the brain-damaged George in Havana, he mistook him for Dick due to their striking physical resemblance and brought him back to Four Winds, where Leslie nursed him for twelve years believing him to be her husband. The truth was finally discovered when Dr. Gilbert Blythe suggested a trephining operation, which restored George Moore's memory and revealed that the real Dick Moore had died thirteen years prior.

label: History
value: Dora and Davy are twins.
unit: Dora and her twin brother Davy were left orphans when their mother, Mary Keith, died of a terminal illness. Marilla Cuthbert took them into Green Gables, where Dora quickly adapted by being exceptionally polite, quiet, and helpful around the house and garden. Unlike her unruly brother Davy, Dora followed instructions easily and avoided mischief, though she was occasionally coerced by Davy into awkward situations. On one occasion, Davy forced her to walk a pigpen fence, causing her to fall into the mud and ruining her clothes. As she grew up at Green Gables, she remained dutiful and neat, inheriting Anne's former bedroom in the porch gable when Anne left for college. At seventeen years old, Dora became courted by Ralph Andrews, a former schoolmate.

unit: Dora and her twin brother Davy were left orphans when their mother, Mary Keith, died of a terminal illness. Marilla Cuthbert took them into Green Gables, where Dora quickly adapted by being exceptionally polite, quiet, and helpful around the house and garden. Unlike her unruly brother Davy, Dora followed instructions easily and avoided mischief, though she was occasionally coerced by Davy into awkward situations. On one occasion, Davy forced her to walk a pigpen fence, causing her to fall into the mud and ruining her clothes. As she grew up at Green Gables, she remained dutiful and neat, inheriting Anne's former bedroom in the porch gable when Anne left for college. At seventeen years old, Dora became courted by Ralph Andrews, a former schoolmate.

label: History
value: Gilbert returned to Avonlea School
unit: Gilbert returned to Avonlea School after spending three years in Alberta with his father. On his first day back, he teased new student Anne Shirley by pulling her red hair and calling her 'Carrots,' prompting her to smash a slate over his head. Though Gilbert immediately apologized, Anne nursed a grudge and refused to speak to him for years, sparking a intense academic rivalry throughout their school days. After graduating from Avonlea School and Queen's Academy, Gilbert taught at the White Sands school for two years, selflessly giving up his application for the Avonlea school so that Anne could remain at Green Gables with Marilla. Later, he attended Redmond College alongside Anne, where he excelled academically, led the Freshman football team to victory, and won the prestigious Cooper Prize and the Senior Class Medal upon graduation. During his Redmond years, he proposed to Anne at Patty's Place but was initially rejected, though he never stopped loving her. After a near-fatal bout with typhoid fever in his final summer, Gilbert and Anne reconciled their feelings upon learning of her love for him. Following his graduation with a B.A. and his medical degree, he accepted his great-uncle's practice at Glen St. Mary and Four Winds Harbor. After a three-year engagement, Gilbert and Anne were married in the orchard at Green Gables.

unit: After the death of his sister in Scottsford, New Brunswick, Mr. Harrison married Emily Scott. Their marriage suffered due to her obsession with neatness and her dislike of his profanely inclined parrot, Ginger; after a clash over the bird, Emily left him. Mr. Harrison then moved to Avonlea and bought Robert Bell's farm next to Green Gables, living as a bachelor with his parrot. He clashed initially with Anne Shirley when her cow broke into his oatfield, but they reconciled after Anne accidentally sold his cow under the impression that it was her own. Anne confessed her mistake and offered her own cow in replacement, winning his friendship. Later, his wife Emily discovered a false newspaper notice hinting at his remarriage and arrived at Avonlea to reunite with him. After Ginger's death in a severe thunderstorm, the couple settled into a tidy, harmonious life together, remaining good neighbors to the Green Gables household.

label: History
value: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea
unit: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school alongside Anne Shirley and Diana Barry. After studying in Miss Stacy's extra class, she attended Queen's Academy, where she excelled in domestic science and obtained a teacher's license. She taught school at Newbridge for two years, earning a place on the School Inspector's Roll of Honor. Jane participated actively in the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, serving as chairman of the committee to paint and shingle the assembly hall. Following her teaching career in Newbridge, she accepted a school position in western Canada. While out West, she became engaged to Edward Inglis, a wealthy Winnipeg businessman originally from England. Jane returned to Avonlea and married Mr. Inglis at her parents' home in a lavish ceremony before embarking on a European wedding tour and settling in Winnipeg.

value: Miss Lavendar is a tiny woman.

label: History
value: Miss Lavendar Lewis spent most of her life living in Echo Lodge.
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis spent most of her life living in a secluded, ivy-covered stone house called Echo Lodge in Grafton. In her youth, she was engaged to Stephen Irving, but the engagement was broken off after a trivial quarrel which her pride and sulkiness prevented her from mending. She subsequently lived for twenty-five years in isolation, maintaining her spirits through imagination, play-acting, and the companionship of her maid, Charlotta the Fourth. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry discovered her home by accident and became close friends with her. Later, Anne introduced Stephen's son, Paul Irving, to her. Learning through Paul's letters that Miss Lavendar was still unmarried, Stephen Irving returned to Prince Edward Island. The two reconciled, were married in her old-fashioned garden, and departed for a new home in Boston, intending to return to Echo Lodge for their summers.

label: Personality
value: Leslie is intense.
unit: Intense, proud, and deeply clannish, Leslie was hardened by years of tragic misfortune into a cold, aloof, and sometimes bitter reserve. Beneath her defensive mantle lies a warm, vivid, and deeply loving nature that blossoms in the company of true friends. She possesses a keen wit, a rich capacity for joy, and a firm, old-fashioned sense of duty and honor. Though once tormented by envy of those with happier lives, she possesses the courage to acknowledge her faults and seek reconciliation.

label: History
value: Leslie grew up on the West farm
unit: Leslie grew up on the West farm in Four Winds. After the tragic deaths of her brother and father, she excelled at Queen's Academy and took up teaching. At sixteen, her mother pressured her into marrying Dick Moore to save their mortgaged farm. Following her mother's death, Dick went to sea and was eventually brought back by Captain Jim as a brain-damaged invalid, whom Leslie dutifully nursed for twelve years. Upon the arrival of Anne and Gilbert Blythe at Four Winds, Leslie formed a deep, albeit initially troubled, friendship with Anne. Encouraged by Dr. Gilbert Blythe, Leslie took her husband to a Montreal hospital for a brain operation. The surgery restored the man's memory, revealing that he was actually Dick's lookalike cousin, George Moore, and that the real Dick Moore had died years earlier in Cuba. Granted her freedom, Leslie returned to Four Winds and eventually confessed her mutual love for writer Owen Ford, whom she agreed to marry.

label: History
value: Jem was born in the early summer.
unit: Jem was born in the early summer at the house of dreams in Four Winds, the second child of Anne and Gilbert Blythe after the loss of his older sister, Joy. He was named James Matthew in honor of Captain Jim Boyd and Matthew Cuthbert. He grew into a healthy, thriving infant, bringing immense happiness to his parents and household after their previous grief. During his infancy, he was adored and cared for by his mother, Susan Baker, Marilla Cuthbert, and neighboring friends like Leslie Moore, Miss Cornelia, and Captain Jim. In the autumn following his first birthday, he moved with his parents and Susan from the house of dreams to the larger Morgan property at Glen St. Mary.

unit: Jem was born in the early summer at the house of dreams in Four Winds, the second child of Anne and Gilbert Blythe after the loss of his older sister, Joy. He was named James Matthew in honor of Captain Jim Boyd and Matthew Cuthbert. He grew into a healthy, thriving infant, bringing immense happiness to his parents and household after their previous grief. During his infancy, he was adored and cared for by his mother, Susan Baker, Marilla Cuthbert, and neighboring friends like Leslie Moore, Miss Cornelia, and Captain Jim. In the autumn following his first birthday, he moved with his parents and Susan from the house of dreams to the larger Morgan property at Glen St. Mary.

value: Marilla is a tall woman.

value: Marilla has narrow experience.

Though outwardly strict, crisp, and undemonstrative, she hides a deep warmth, maternal tenderness, and an underlying sense of humor. She holds strongly to her convictions and can be stubborn, yet she possesses the humility to admit her mistakes and soften her sternness when guided by love.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet, solitary life at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet, solitary life at Green Gables with her brother Matthew until they decided to adopt an orphan boy to assist on the farm. By a mistake in the message, an eleven-year-old girl, Anne Shirley, was brought to them instead. Although Marilla initially intended to return the child, she was persuaded by Matthew's silent persistence and her own growing pity to keep her. Over the years, Marilla conscientiously undertook Anne's upbringing, attempting to curb her wild imagination and garrulous nature while secretly falling deeply in love with her. When Matthew died suddenly, Marilla faced the prospect of selling Green Gables due to her failing eyesight, but Anne gave up her college scholarship to stay and help her. Marilla's eyes later improved sufficiently to avert blindness, and she took in her distant relative's orphaned twins, Davy and Dora Keith, as well as her lifelong friend Mrs. Rachel Lynde, after the death of Thomas Lynde. Years later, Marilla joyfully gave her consent and blessing to Anne's marriage to Gilbert Blythe, opening Green Gables to its very first wedding.

value: Marshall Elliott is an intense man.
unit: Marshall Elliott is an intense, fiery-tempered man known for his extreme stubbornness and fierce partisan loyalty. Despite his crusty demeanor and outbursts of anger, he possesses a witty, intelligent, and well-read mind, making him an engaging storyteller. He holds a deep chivalrous streak, firmly refusing to tolerate any derogatory remarks about women. Behind his stubborn eccentricities lies a kind, generous nature and an appreciation for spunk in others.

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott grew up in Four Winds.
unit: Marshall Elliott grew up in Four Winds as a staunch Liberal. In his youth, he courted Ellen West, but the relationship ended in a bitter rift. During a heated general election fifteen years before the events of the Four Winds narrative, he publicly swore that he would not cut his hair or shave his beard until the Liberal party gained power. He adhered to this vow for a decade and a half, growing a massive mane and beard that made him an eccentric figure in the district. After the Liberals won the federal election, he immediately woke up the local barber in the middle of the night to shave his beard and trim his hair. Following his physical transformation, he renewed his courtship of Ellen West and persuaded her to marry him, ultimately moving to her farm to live together.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert is an aging farmer.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert, an aging farmer living at Green Gables with his sister Marilla, decided to adopt an orphan boy to assist with farm work. Upon driving to the station, he discovered that an eleven-year-old girl, Anne Shirley, had been sent by mistake. Too shy to explain the error, Matthew brought her home and quickly became fond of her chatter and vibrant spirit, persuading Marilla to keep her. Throughout Anne's upbringing, Matthew acted as her indulgent ally, buying her a dress with puffed sleeves for Christmas and supporting her educational ambitions. As his health declined due to heart spells, he continued to work hard on the farm. After Anne graduated from Queen's Academy with top honors, Matthew died suddenly of a heart attack upon reading of the failure of the Abbey Bank, where his savings were kept.

label: History
value: Owen Ford came to Four Winds to recover his health.
unit: Owen Ford came to Four Winds to recover his health after a bout of typhoid fever and boarded with Leslie Moore at the gray house up the brook. Introduced to Captain Jim by Anne Blythe, he discovered Captain Jim's 'life-book' of sea adventures and resolved to use it as the basis for his novel. During his time at Four Winds, he collaborated closely with Captain Jim and spent his afternoons and evenings with Anne, Gilbert, and Leslie, falling deeply in love with Leslie. Believing Leslie to be irrevocably tied to her brain-damaged husband, Dick Moore, he suffered quietly and prepared to leave Four Winds forever. However, after Gilbert urged an operation for Dick, it was revealed that 'Dick' was actually his cousin George Moore and that the real Dick had died years prior. After Leslie became a free woman, Owen returned to Four Winds the following summer. He proposed to Leslie in Anne's garden, and the two became engaged to be married.

Following their marriage, Paul moved back to Boston with his father and new mother. Years later, at sixteen, he returned for a summer visit to Echo Lodge and promised to visit Anne at Four Winds after completing two years of study abroad.

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon first met Anne Shirley
unit: Philippa Gordon first met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant in Old St. John's Cemetery during her Freshman year at Redmond College. Coming from a wealthy family in Bolingbroke, she quickly befriended them and brought them into her social circle. She was courted by numerous suitors, particularly two hometown admirers named Alec and Alonzo, whom she struggled to choose between due to her extreme indecisiveness. During her college years, Philippa moved into Patty's Place with Anne, Priscilla, Stella, and Aunt Jamesina. While vacationing at Prospect Point, she met Jonas Blake, a poor divinity student, and fell deeply in love with him. Overcoming her former desire for wealth and luxury, she accepted Jonas's proposal and committed herself to becoming a minister's wife. She graduated from Redmond with Honors in Mathematics alongside her friends.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster of the Avonlea school
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster of the Avonlea school, where he spent most of his time focusing on his eldest pupils, particularly Prissy Andrews, whom he courted. During his tenure, he frequently punished students, including holding up Anne Shirley's slate to humiliate her for bad spelling, forcing her to stand before the blackboard after she broke her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head, and making her sit with Gilbert as a punishment for being late. During a local entertainment for the Avonlea Debating Club, he recited Mark Antony's oration over the body of Caesar. At the end of June, he gave a farewell speech to the school and departed his position, having secured the job through his uncle's influence as a trustee.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Priscilla Grant previously attended Queen's Academy with Anne Shirley and later taught at the Carmody school for a time before accepting a position at her own home school. After two years of teaching, she entered Redmond College as a Sophomore, boarding initially in Kingsport. While in college, she and Anne met Philippa Gordon in Old St. John's Cemetery, becoming close friends with her. Tired of boarding, Priscilla joined Anne, Stella Maynard, and Philippa in renting Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue for their remaining college years, with her Aunt Jamesina acting as housekeeper. During her summer vacation, Priscilla brought her aunt, the noted author Charlotte E. Morgan, to visit Anne at Green Gables. At Redmond, Priscilla devoted herself to classics, graduating with Honors in her Senior year. Following graduation, she went to Japan to work in the mission field.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived for many years in Lynde's Hollow
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived for many years in Lynde's Hollow with her husband Thomas, managing her household, running the Sewing Circle, helping with the Sunday School, and supporting church missions. When Matthew Cuthbert drove past her house in a best suit, her curiosity led her to visit Green Gables, where she learned the Cuthberts intended to adopt an orphan boy. Upon meeting the newly arrived Anne Shirley, Rachel's blunt criticism of her appearance provoked a fiery outburst from the girl, though she later accepted Anne's dramatic apology and grew fond of her. Throughout Anne's school and college years, Mrs. Rachel frequently gave advice on her upbringing, church affairs, and local gossip. When her husband Thomas fell ill, she nursed him faithfully until his death. Following his passing and the necessity to sell their mortgaged farm, she accepted Marilla's invitation to move into Green Gables, taking up residence in the renovated north gable room while helping Marilla manage the house and twins.

Upon meeting the newly arrived Anne Shirley, Rachel's blunt criticism of her appearance provoked a fiery outburst from the girl, though she later accepted Anne's dramatic apology and grew fond of her. Throughout Anne's school and college years, Mrs. Rachel frequently gave advice on her upbringing, church affairs, and local gossip. When her husband Thomas fell ill, she nursed him faithfully until his death. Following his passing and the necessity to sell their mortgaged farm, she accepted Marilla's invitation to move into Green Gables, taking up residence in the renovated north gable room while helping Marilla manage the house and twins.

label: History
value: Jonas Blake attended Redmond College
unit: Jonas Blake attended Redmond College and St. Columbia to prepare for the ministry. While spending a summer in charge of the Prospect Point Mission Church, he met Philippa Gordon at his boardinghouse. Despite his ungainly appearance, his earnestness, spiritual depth, and beautiful preaching won her affection. After completing his theological studies, he took charge of a mission church on Patterson Street in the slums. He eventually married Philippa in June following her graduation, and later attended the wedding of Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe at Green Gables, where he delivered a moving prayer. Afterwards, he and Philippa settled into their new life and ministry together.

label: History
value: Roy Gardner completed his Freshman year at Redmond College.
unit: Roy Gardner completed his Freshman and Sophomore years at Redmond College before taking a two-year hiatus to travel throughout Europe with his mother for her health. Upon returning to Kingsport to resume his Junior year at Redmond, he met Anne Shirley in the park during a heavy November rainstorm when her umbrella turned inside out. He rescued her under a pavilion and accompanied her home, subsequently sending her a dozen roses and courting her intensely throughout their remaining college years. During their Senior year, his mother and sisters called upon Anne, cementing his family's acceptance of her. On the eve of their departure from Redmond, Roy took Anne to the park pavilion where they first met and formally proposed marriage. To his shock, Anne rejected him, realizing she did not truly love him. Heartbroken, Roy bade her farewell, believing his life was ruined.

label: History
value: Ruby grew up in Avonlea
unit: Ruby grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school, where she became a member of the girls' Story Club and a classmate of Anne Shirley. After finishing school, she studied at Queen's Academy alongside Anne and her friends, obtaining her teacher's license. She subsequently taught at Carmody, where she was known for her numerous flirtations and admirers. Ruby later accepted the White Sands school, but contracted a severe attack of congestion during the winter which developed into galloping consumption. Unable to teach, she returned home to Avonlea for her final summer. For months she refused to acknowledge her illness, continuing to dress up and talk gaily of her beaus. However, shortly before her death, she broke down to Anne, confessing her deep fear of dying and leaving the earthly life she loved. She died peacefully in her sleep at the age of nineteen, leaving behind a deep impression of her transformed beauty and a lingering memory among her old schoolmates.

Ruby later accepted the White Sands school, but contracted a severe attack of congestion during the winter which developed into galloping consumption. However, shortly before her death, she broke down to Anne, confessing her deep fear of dying and leaving the earthly life she loved. She died peacefully in her sleep at the age of nineteen, leaving behind a deep impression of her transformed beauty and a lingering memory among her old schoolmates.

label: History
value: Miss Stacy was hired as the new lady teacher for Avonlea school
unit: Miss Stacy was hired as the new lady teacher for Avonlea school, replacing Mr. Phillips. Upon taking her position in the autumn, she quickly introduced new educational methods, including physical culture exercises, field afternoons in the woods to study nature, and Friday afternoon recitations. In November, she organized a student concert on Christmas Night to raise funds for a schoolhouse flag. Later, she formed an advanced class to prepare her students for the Entrance examination to Queen's Academy, giving them extra lessons for an hour after school. Although offered a position in her home district, she chose to stay in Avonlea to see her students through their examinations. After seeing them successfully through, she later married and moved to California.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy with Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Ruby Gillis, where she was part of their story-writing club. After completing her course at Queen's, she taught in a country school for two years, an experience she found full of trials and demanding parents. Eager to further her education and escape boarding, she decided to attend Redmond College, entering as a Sophomore. She proposed to Anne and Priscilla that they rent a house together along with her Aunt Jamesina as housekeeper. They successfully leased Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue, where she lived happily with Anne, Priscilla, Philippa Gordon, and Aunt Jamesina throughout her remaining college years. Stella completed her Arts course at Redmond, achieving a solid all-round academic standing at graduation, and subsequently accepted a position teaching in Vancouver.

label: History
value: Susan Baker was employed as the housekeeper at Green Gables.
unit: Susan Baker was employed as the housekeeper at Green Gables and later moved to Ingleside with Dr. Gilbert Blythe and Anne. When Anne fell severely ill after the birth of her son Shirley, Susan nursed and cared for the baby, claiming him as her own and developing an intense maternal devotion to him. She managed the Ingleside household with dedication, keeping it in order and preparing meals for the family. Susan remained a steadfast presence through all the joys and sorrows of the Blythe family, including the tragic loss of Anne's firstborn child, Joy. When Anne and Gilbert moved from their house of dreams to the Glen St. Mary home, Susan cheerfully accompanied them to manage their larger residence.
